findings.resolution: Both languages now say symptoms OR signs, preserving the independent alternative to volume criteria. Confirmed against CMA definition47 and the claim/body binding.

section_conclusions.assessment: Definitions, normal-lochia distinction and timing match attributed UK/US patient material; no universal milliliter definition implied.
Atony, retained tissue, trauma, placenta and coagulation mechanisms and planning factors supported; no-risk history does not exclude PPH.
Heavy bleeding independently triggers emergency help; pad/clot examples do not delay action. Safe accompaniment/transport is practical support, not an invented clinical numeric threshold.
Acute emergency, urgent delayed deterioration and planned recovery are separated. Recent birth should be reported; unavailable maternity team does not delay emergency assessment.

WHO treatment trigger, Chinese traditional definition and older UK classification kept distinct. OR criterion corrected; vaginal-evidence and CS limitations explicit; numbers are not home waiting targets.
Normal lochia and delayed infection/retained tissue differentiated. New chest/breathing/fainting symptoms are not explained away as ordinary anemia or tiredness.
Coordinated first measures, cause-specific repair/removal and escalation supported without individualized drug or procedure instructions.
Prevention versus active treatment and IV TXA birth-time3h window preserved. Hypertension and asthma conditions explicit; NICE avoidance and SmPC caution not conflated.

Food after stabilization supports recovery; significant anemia may require iron therapy. Unsupported egg example removed. Team-cleared intake is a practical perioperative condition, not a new fasting prescription.
Observation records, household assistance and gradual recovery are practical low-risk advice, not falsely quantified therapies. Breastfeeding support does not delay warning-sign care.
Preexisting anemia, placental/coagulation issues, anticoagulants, transfusion preferences, asthma and hypertension appropriately affect preparation and choices.
Physical and emotional recovery, anemia follow-up and future-birth planning supported. Nightmares/difficulty coping are examples for asking support, not diagnostic criteria or incidence claims.
Anemia and severe circulatory/organ injury distinguished. Clot-risk prevention specifically follows control of bleeding and correction of coagulopathy; no unsupervised anticoagulant adjustment.
Antenatal preparation, professional birth care and recognition presented without zero-risk promise or duplicating full rare-disease coverage.

evidence_boundaries: Separate authoring groups do not prove separate underlying studies. EBCOG comments on WHO with FIGO role overlap; Cochrane summaries share authors and WHO funding; CMA uses international guidance.
East Kent discloses Ontario adaptation and RCOG references. Ordinary recovery advice can have one adequate source; it is not promoted into independent efficacy evidence.

RCOG2016 is under review. Current drug decisions are additionally bound to2023/2025 guidelines or the specific product label. NATA access is limited to the actual official indexed thromboprophylaxis passage.

Region-attributed definitions and institutional intervention thresholds are not patient self-diagnosis tools. Neonatal, placental and clotting subtypes do not automatically gain complete coverage from this overview.
